Apple root rot, collar rot and dying trees

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Most apple tree deaths in India come from three causes: white root rot (Dematophora necatrix) in waterlogged monsoon soil, collar rot (Phytophthora cactorum) on MM.106 in clay, and untreated apple replant disease. All three start with poor drainage or the wrong site. Early cases can be saved by draining water away, exposing and cleaning the root collar, copper paste and a drench recommended by your university (ICAR-CITH, SKUAST-K).

Which one is killing your trees?

ProblemWhat you seeWhenMain cause
White root rotSparse, small, yellow leaves, then the tree collapses; dig the roots: brown rotten roots covered in white cottony fungusWorst in June–SeptemberWaterlogged soil, hillside runoff
Collar rotSlimy reddish-brown bark rot right at the soil lineWet seasonsMM.106 in clay or wet soil; buried graft union
Canker and diebackCracked, sunken bark; branches dying back from pruning stubsAny timeUnsealed pruning cuts and stubs (Botryosphaeria, Diplodia)
Apple replant diseaseYoung trees in old apple land stay stunted for yearsFirst 1–3 yearsFungi, nematodes and soil fatigue in old apple soil
Woolly aphid on rootsWhite wool on twigs; galls on roots; stunted treesSpring to autumnSusceptible rootstock (seedling, M.9, M.7)

Saving trees with white root rot or collar rot

  1. Drain the water: dig cut-off ditches above the orchard on slopes so runoff does not reach the trees; plant on raised mounds where soil stays wet.
  2. Keep the graft union 15–20 cm above the soil and keep a 60 cm undisturbed basin around the trunk.
  3. Expose the collar and main roots in November–December, cut away dead roots and rotten bark, and paint with copper oxychloride or Bordeaux paste.
  4. Drench the root zone in April, June, July and September as per the ICAR / state university protocol: for white root rot, carbendazim + mancozeb or a Trichoderma + Pseudomonas bio-drench; for collar rot, metalaxyl-M + mancozeb or copper oxychloride with Trichoderma. Doses as per the registered label.
  5. Remove dead trees with as many roots as possible and do not replant in the same pit without treating the soil.

Replanting old apple land

  • Shift new pits into the old alleyways, away from old root zones.
  • Fallow with mustard or marigold, or solarise the soil under clear plastic in summer.
  • Fill pits with virgin topsoil, well-rotted FYM and a bio-consortium of VAM (AMF), Trichoderma and Pseudomonas; SKUAST-K (2024) found this strongly cut replant deaths.
  • Use Geneva rootstocks (G.11, G.41, G.214) where available: bred for replant tolerance.

Prevent canker dieback

Seal every pruning cut over 2.5 cm the same day with copper paste, cut cankers 15 cm into healthy wood, sterilise tools with 70% ethanol, whitewash trunks in November and give a post-harvest copper spray. Pruning guide.

Questions farmers ask

Why are my apple trees dying?

Most often white root rot in waterlogged monsoon soil, collar rot on MM.106 in clay, canker from unsealed pruning cuts, or replant disease in old apple land.

How do I identify white root rot in apple?

Leaves become sparse, small and yellow; dig at the roots: rotten brown roots covered with white cottony fungus, mostly in June–September.

How do I treat collar rot in apple?

Improve drainage, keep the graft 15–20 cm above soil, scrape rotten bark and paint with Bordeaux paste, and drench as per your university protocol.

Can I plant new apple trees where old ones died?

Not directly. Move pits to the old alleyways or treat the soil (fallow or solarise, fresh topsoil, FYM, VAM + Trichoderma + Pseudomonas) and use replant-tolerant rootstocks if available.
